## Summary

A real estate client wanted a model that predicts a home's sale price from its listing details. I cleaned 20,000 King County (Seattle area) sales, engineered features, and trained gradient-boosted trees with **XGBoost**. The model was then scored on a hidden holdout set as a class competition.

| Model version | Test RMSE | Test R² |
|---|---|---|
| Engineered features + geographic clusters | $136,744 | 0.88 |
| **Cleaned outliers + date features (final)** | **$113,938** | **0.90** |

## Approach

**1. Cleaning.** I parsed the sale date into year and month, dropped ID columns, and removed implausible records: more than 15 bedrooms, bathroom counts outside 0.5–5.5, and extreme living and lot sizes.

**2. Feature engineering.** I used log transforms of square footage, living-to-lot and above-to-basement ratios, house age, years since renovation, and a renovation flag. K-means clusters on latitude and longitude capture neighborhood effects.

**3. Model.** I used an XGBoost regressor with an 80/20 train/test split, then ran the same cleaning function on the holdout set so the training and scoring data stay consistent.

```python
def clean_housing(housing):
    housing['datetime'] = housing['date'].str.split('T').str[0]
    housing = housing.assign(
        year=housing['datetime'].str[0:4].astype(int),
        month=housing['datetime'].str[4:6].astype(int),
    ).drop(columns=['date', 'datetime', 'id'])

    clean = housing[housing['bedrooms'] <= 15]
    clean = clean[(clean['bathrooms'] <= 5.5) & (clean['bathrooms'] >= .5)]
    clean = clean[clean['sqft_living'] <= 8670]
    clean = clean[clean['sqft_lot'] <= 500000]
    return clean

model = XGBRegressor()
model.fit(X_train, y_train)
predictions = model.predict(X_test)
```

## What I learned

Removing a small number of extreme listings improved the model more than adding extra engineered features did, cutting RMSE by about $23,000. Bundling the cleaning steps into a single function also made it simple to score new holdout files without mismatched columns.
